desc:
Encoding. A non-negative integer is stored as an array of its decimal digits, most significant digit first, one digit per element, with no leading zeros; the number zero is stored as [0]. Results use the same format. The numbers can have thousands of digits, so you cannot convert a whole array into one machine integer.

Return the digit array of |a - b|, the absolute difference of the two numbers. If the numbers are equal, return [0].

Example: a = [1,0,0,0], b = [9,9,9] gives [1]. Example: a = [2,5], b = [7,1] gives [4,6].
constraints: No leading zeros, except for the number zero stored as [0]
hints: Subtraction on paper only works when you subtract the smaller number from the larger one. Decide which is which first.
Without leading zeros, a longer array is a larger number. For equal lengths, compare the digits from the left.
Subtract the digits from the right with a borrow flag: if x - y - borrow is negative, add 10 and set borrow to 1. The result can start with zeros, so drop them (keep one digit).
editorial: First order the operands. Because there are no leading zeros, the array with more digits is larger; when both lengths are equal the lexicographic comparison of the arrays equals the numeric comparison.

Then do column subtraction from the right with a borrow. The larger number never runs out of digits before the smaller one, and since big ≥ small the final borrow is always 0. Leading zeros created by cancellation (as in 1000 - 999) are removed at the end, leaving a single 0 for equal inputs. Linear time.
